sections.content: How many people stayed in Bournemouth after gaining qualifications?

Bournemouth is a large town in the South West. Bournemouth also has a university.

Bournemouth has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Bournemouth ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 6,575 state-school pupils from Bournemouth who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 1,850 (28%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 2,090 (32%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Bournemouth to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Bournemouth's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Bournemouth in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Bournemouth move to?

Of Bournemouth's graduates, 705 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 65 of those graduates (9%) were living fairly locally, in the Bournemouth travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Bournemouth's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 470 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 95 of those qualified non-graduates (20%) were living fairly locally, in the Bournemouth travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Bournemouth's GCSE cohort:

  • 530 graduates left the South West
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 195 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the South West
  • the most common region they moved to was the South East

In 2018 to 2019, 55% of graduates and 38% of qualified non-graduates living in Bournemouth had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 2,470 graduates and 2,515 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Bournemouth. This is compared with the 1,850 graduates and 2,090 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 45% of the graduates had also lived in Bournemouth as GCSE pupils, while 55% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Bournemouth in 2018 to 2019, 62% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 38% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
